dedupe_keys.name: costliest u s hailstorms dataset radar hail swaths and storm reports 1995 2017 university at albany

description: The Costliest U.S. Hailstorms dataset gives radar-derived swaths and storm reports for about 55 of the most damaging hailstorms to hit US metropolitan areas between 1995 and 2017, grouped into extreme events above US$1 billion in losses, major events of US$501 million to 1 billion and significant events of US$100 to 500 million. Brian Tang of the University at Albany built it with sponsorship from the Risk Prediction Initiative, choosing events mainly from NCEI property loss data adjusted to 2017 dollars and supplemented from journal articles and insurance organisations. Each event file holds gridded reflectivity, hail kinetic energy and maximum estimated size of hail, plus integrated kinetic energy and time-maximum MESH swaths smoothed by optical flow interpolation between scans. Format and access: CF-compliant NetCDF4 radar files and CSV Storm Prediction Center hail and wind reports per event, from a table on the page; coverage is US metropolitan areas. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: radar is missing for four cases and incomplete for five, loss data do not separate wind from hail, and storms far from or near the radar are poorly sampled. It supports hazard exposure and resilience studies, for example moving swaths over insured assets to estimate losses. Related catalogue records are the NOAA Storm Events Database and the Swiss radar crop hail damage model.
